summary: The note describes a growing local trend of green exercise, meaning physical activity in natural settings, which has spread since September 2023. It covers trainer-led park workouts, research on psychological benefits, fitness festivals and eco-races, school and corporate programs, and a resulting boom in the local fitness economy.
one_line: Green exercise in local parks is booming since September 2023, spanning trainers, festivals, eco-races, schools, workplaces and the outdoor fitness economy.
key_facts: Green exercise is defined as physical exercise conducted in natural environments, and has been growing among locals since September 2023.
Marlon Griffith, a certified personal trainer and outdoor enthusiast, launched a series of 'Parks and Reps' workout sessions in the city's green spaces in early October.
Griffith's clients are of all ages and fitness levels and exercise together in public parks, doing lunges, squats and jogging.
Dr. Samantha Carter, who holds a PhD in Environmental Psychology, shared her insights on green exercise on November 5th.
Carter says green exercise is a multisensory experience that can enhance mood, reduce stress and improve self-esteem, and that nature can also sharpen focus and mental acuity.
Local fitness festivals began in November, offering yoga under the sky, grass boot camps and woodland trail running events.
The 'Leaves of Change Relay Race' was organized on December 12th by environmental activist group EcoStride, combining racing with maintaining the city's greenery.
Eco-friendly races prioritize sustainability, often leaving behind no carbon footprint.
Physical Education teacher Mr. Jacob Perez began incorporating outdoor circuits and nature walks into his curriculum since the school year started in September.
Schoolyard gardens and modified sports activities in nearby parks are encouraging children to be active while respecting the environment.
ThriveTech reported improved employee engagement and energy levels after moving wellness activities to local green hubs, according to HR manager Lisa Ford in a company-wide email last September.
Corporate wellness programs increasingly host walking meetings, walking groups and outdoor team-building exercises to reduce workplace stress.
Outdoor and sports stores reported significant sales increases in hydration packs, trail shoes and eco-friendly workout gear.
Small businesses are supplying post-workout snacks at park kiosks, pop-up smoothie bars and bike rental services.
